title: LFM2.5 Q4_0 Checkpoints from Quantization-Aware Distillation
summary: LiquidAI releases Q4_0 GGUF checkpoints for LFM2.5 models (230M, 350M, 1.2B-Instruct, and 2.6B) using Quantization-Aware Distillation (QAD). This method recovers 97% of BF16 accuracy lost during quantization while maintaining the speed and memory efficiency of 4-bit models. Benchmarks show QAD checkpoints outperform traditional post-training quantization (PTQ) across reasoning, instruction-following, tool use, and agentic tasks. The models are optimized for edge deployment on devices like MacBook Pro, Raspberry Pi 5, and Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra.
key_points: Quantization-Aware Distillation (QAD) is used to train 4-bit checkpoints for LFM2.5 models, recovering 97% of BF16 accuracy lost during quantization.
QAD checkpoints maintain the same memory footprint and speed as native Q4_0 GGUFs while significantly improving performance over post-training quantization (PTQ).
Benchmark results show QAD checkpoints retain 96.5% to 97.4% of their BF16 baseline performance across tasks like GPQA Diamond, MMLU-Pro, IFEval, and GSM8K/AIME25.
The 230M and 350M QAD Q4_0 checkpoints match Q5_K_M quality with 4-33% higher decode throughput, while the 1.2B and 2.6B checkpoints match Q4_K_M quality with 3-14% higher throughput.
QAD checkpoints are optimized for edge deployment, with tested performance on devices like MacBook Pro (GPU), Raspberry Pi 5 (Arm CPU), and Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra (Arm CPU).
The models are available in GGUF format and can be used with tools like `llama.cpp` for inference.
Links to the checkpoints are provided for LFM2.5-230M, LFM2.5-350M, LFM2.5-1.2B-Instruct, and LFM2.5-2.6B.
